Note what this question needs, because the two possible answers cost very different amounts.
To answer yes you need exactly ONE listing that meets the condition. Name it and stop. Nothing is gained by finding a second.
To answer no you must have ruled out every listing that could meet it.
1. Read the advertised price of every listing from the search results first. That price is the cheapest option that listing can sell, so nothing it can sell costs less.
2. Open listings in ascending order of advertised price. For each one, choose size M, then look at the page again and read the price it now shows. The price a listing shows before you choose is its cheapest option that can be bought, not necessarily the one asked about, and the reply to choosing an option does not show the new price. Then check whether that option can actually be bought. An option can be listed and still be unavailable, in which case it is shown as disabled or greyed out and cannot be chosen from the menu, so it has no price you can use.
3. If the option is available and the price you read is below $12.00, you are finished. Answer yes, name that listing and the price you read, and stop immediately. Do not open any others to confirm.
4. Skip every unopened listing whose advertised price is at or above $12.00. Nothing it can sell costs less than its advertised price, so it cannot meet the condition.
5. Only when every listing advertised below $12.00 has been opened and none meets the condition may you answer no.
In your answer, say how many listings you opened and which one settled it, or that none of those that could meet the condition did. Stopping after one opening, when that listing meets the condition, is the correct outcome here, not a sign that you did too little.
Important: the figure this bound produces is a limit used only to decide what to skip. It is not a price read for the option asked about, and must never appear in your answer as one. Only report a price you read from a listing you opened, for the exact option asked about, read after that option was chosen. Never pair an advertised price with an option unless you saw that price shown while that option was chosen.
A size's label in the menu can carry promotional or stock text; the price is the one shown after the size is chosen, and a label's claim is not a checked fact.

result.final: Yes. Haldane Apparel sells a Wexcombe Midweight Jersey Tee in size M for $11.92 (shown with size M selected; listed at http://localhost:7770/igr-tcl-40.html), which is available to buy and under $12.00. I opened all 5 listings advertised below $12.00 (Dovercourt Apparel $10.13, Whitlock Outfitters $11.09, Carnforth Textile Company $11.38, Oakfield Textile Company $11.69, Haldane Apparel $11.92); the 5th, Haldane Apparel, settled it. The other 4 could not meet the condition (Dovercourt offers no M; Whitlock's M is disabled; Carnforth's M is $13.02; Oakfield's M is disabled). The 40 listings advertising $12.00 or more were skipped since nothing they sell can cost less than their advertised price.
